channel.title: Midnight blog - en
channel.description: 记录软件从需求、架构设计、开发、测试到发布、运维与持续改进的工程实践，讨论具体约束、方案取舍和验证方法。AI 是工具链的一部分。 | Language: en

item.title: Downloading an artifact is not proof it is the approved build
item.description: Bind approval to a specific workflow run and artifact digest, then verify that same object at deployment.

item.title: When architecture changes, keep the superseded ADR
item.description: Preserve the old decision, link its replacement, and separate architectural intent from migration completion.

item.title: No CSP reports does not prove an enforcement policy is ready
item.description: Verify reporting and workflow coverage before enforcing CSP; an empty report stream is not proof of safety.

item.title: Is SameSite alone enough to prevent CSRF?
item.description: Evaluate SameSite against the application threat model and protect state-changing requests with explicit checks.

item.title: A Docker secret mount cannot prevent a command from leaking its input
item.description: Secret mounts protect a build input channel; inspect commands, output files and caches for copied credentials.

item.title: Keep diagnostic evidence without creating a second sensitive database
item.description: Log decisions and correlation identifiers while controlling sensitive fields, access and retention.

item.title: A dialog can close while leaving keyboard users lost
item.description: Define dialog entry, contained keyboard navigation and the next focus destination, matching semantics to behavior.

item.title: Does readOnly in OpenAPI actually prevent a write?
item.description: In OpenAPI 3.1.1, readOnly is an annotation; define and verify the actual server-side write policy.

item.title: Tail sampling cannot recover traces already discarded upstream
item.description: Tail sampling selects received traces; upstream drops, routing and decision windows still constrain error coverage.

item.title: Row locks can still deadlock: order resources across every entry point
item.description: Prevent PostgreSQL deadlocks with consistent resource ordering across writers, and retry at the transaction boundary.

item.title: A JSONB GIN index does not support every query shape
item.description: Match PostgreSQL JSONB operator classes and indexed expressions to real queries before evaluating cost.

item.title: Pagination needs a unique order and a cross-page consistency policy
item.description: Use a unique order for PostgreSQL pagination, and define what concurrent changes may do between pages.

item.title: Why can a unique column still contain multiple NULLs?
item.description: PostgreSQL 18 treats NULLs as distinct in unique constraints by default; choose semantics before enforcing identity.

item.title: More clicks, fewer completed tasks? Define the denominator first
item.description: Define attempts, completion and observation windows before interpreting a rise in product clicks.

item.title: One metric label per order turns monitoring into an event database
item.description: Budget label combinations before exposing metrics, and keep unbounded event identities in suitable diagnostic storage.

item.title: Promise.all rejection does not cancel the remaining work
item.description: Promise.all aggregates outcomes; cancellation, compensation and complete result collection need separate policies.

item.title: Terraform state locking does not freeze the cloud
item.description: State locking coordinates a state backend, not every cloud writer; establish ownership before clearing a lock.

item.title: A timestamp offset cannot fully express “every day at nine”
item.description: Store an occurrence separately from recurring calendar intent, and define how local-time ambiguities are handled.

item.title: Image uploads need more than extension and MIME checks
item.description: Quarantine untrusted uploads and review parsing, storage and retrieval permissions as well as file type.

item.title: A smooth demo does not prove usability: write tasks without giving the answer
item.description: Test the goal without giving away the route, and distinguish independent completion from moderator assistance.

item.title: A Dependency Cache Hit Is Not Proof of a Valid Release
item.description: Treat dependency caches as disposable acceleration inputs while preserving lockfile checks and artifact provenance.

item.title: Two Deployments Overlap: Should the Lock Follow the Branch or the Environment?
item.description: Coordinate deployment writers around the target environment and verify final state after cancellation or overlapping runs.

item.title: If a Workflow Does Not Pass a Token, Can an Action Still Access It?
item.description: Limit GITHUB_TOKEN permissions per job and inspect implicit token access before trusting build and publication boundaries.

item.title: Both Saves Succeeded: Why Did One Editor Lose Their Changes?
item.description: Combine strong ETags with atomic version checks and a conflict workflow that preserves unsaved edits.

item.title: Can a Timed-Out Request Be Retried? Define the Business Idempotency Boundary
item.description: Define stable intent and durable deduplication before retrying an order whose outcome is unknown.

item.title: Search Results Went Backward: Cancellation Also Needs a State-Commit Guard
item.description: Combine request cancellation with identity guards on results and errors so older search responses cannot replace current intent.

item.title: Why Does no-cache Still Leave Cached Files?
item.description: Distinguish no-cache from no-store and private by checking validation and reuse across the actual delivery chain.

item.title: Does Replacing Order Numbers with UUIDs Prevent Unauthorized Access?
item.description: Keep object-level authorization independent of UUID guessability across downloads and asynchronous results.

item.title: Users Say They Would Use It: Ask About the Last Real Task First
item.description: Use recent task evidence to test product assumptions without confusing polite agreement with demand.

item.title: Database Slowness Restarts Every Pod: Is the Probe Asking the Wrong Question?
item.description: Match Kubernetes startup and readiness checks to their actions while reserving liveness restarts for appropriate failures.

item.title: The Node Is Idle: Why Is the Container Still Slow?
item.description: Separate Kubernetes requests from runtime limits and correlate container constraints with queues and business latency.

item.title: preStop Is Configured but Requests Still Fail: Budget the Whole Shutdown
item.description: Budget Kubernetes termination across hooks and in-flight work with observable completion rather than fixed sleep.

item.title: Why Should Customer Email Not Go Straight into OpenTelemetry Baggage?
item.description: Separate OpenTelemetry Baggage propagation from telemetry storage and keep sensitive data and authorization outside its trust.

item.title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY Is Still Waiting: What Should a Release Check?
item.description: Plan PostgreSQL 18 concurrent index builds around transaction waits and validity rather than command completion alone.

item.title: A Query Is Slow: Check Row Estimates Before Adding an Index
item.description: Locate row-estimate errors and actual execution work in PostgreSQL 18 before choosing an index or query rewrite.

item.title: Both Transactions Committed: Why Did the Business Invariant Fail?
item.description: Protect PostgreSQL 18 business invariants with suitable concurrency controls and bounded whole-transaction retries.

item.title: The Backup Job Is Green: Why Does Recovery Still Fail?
item.description: Validate PostgreSQL 18 recovery through roles and restored business behavior instead of a successful backup-job status.

item.title: The Database Committed but the Notification Failed: Define the Handoff
item.description: Use a transactional outbox to make handoff recoverable while defining worker ownership and duplicate delivery handling.

item.title: The Key Was Deleted from Git: Why Is the Incident Not Over?
item.description: Verify replacement access and old-credential rejection across declared consumers instead of relying on source deletion.

item.title: A Server Fetches User URLs: Why Is Domain Validation Not Enough?
item.description: Bound server-side URL fetching through destination policy and redirect checks backed by controlled network egress.

item.title: A successful deployment is not a verified release
item.description: Separate source, artifacts, deployment, and user outcomes; rehearse rollback with data compatibility in mind.

item.title: “Support export” is not an acceptance criterion
item.description: Use an export workflow to separate acceptance scenarios, interface boundaries, and architecture decisions.

item.title: Green tests are not enough: design quality gates around failure paths
item.description: Prioritize logic, integration, end-to-end, security, and accessibility checks by the failures they detect.

item.title: Low CPU, failed users: connect service indicators to incident learning
item.description: Distinguish accepted requests from completed jobs, define indicator populations, and make incident actions verifiable.

item.title: Complete Guide to Midnight Theme Configuration
item.description: A practical guide to hexo-theme-midnight v0.1.16 configuration, covering appearance, navigation, i18n, comments, SEO, analytics, homepage modules, and inner pages.

item.title: JD's Nirvana Project: The Social and Business Value of Blue-Collar Reskilling in the AI Era
item.description: A balanced analysis of JD.com's reported Nirvana Project, covering its social value for blue-collar workers and its commercial value for robot maintenance, service networks, and physical-world operations.

item.title: Harness Engineering Explained: The Reliability Layer for AI Agents
item.description: A practical guide to Harness Engineering for AI Agents, covering how it differs from Prompt Engineering, Context Engineering, and agent runtimes, and how constraints, tools, feedback, validation, and sandboxes make agents reliable.

item.title: AI Agent Implementation Guide: From Chatbots to Auditable Workflows
item.description: A practical AI Agent implementation guide for developers and technical teams, covering 2026 agent engineering trends, MCP, tool use, sandboxes, identity, audit logs, and governance.
